2I.9 Backsliding from God's ways causes punishment and the loss of His protection.

precepts.text: Verily I will cause the enemy to entreat thee well in the time of evil; that favor took Joseph from prison to governor.
precepts.point: Jacob knew there was corn in Egypt because Joseph had already told Pharaoh exactly what to do to save up in the time of tribulation; when Jacob heard, he sent out the fathers. Applying these attributes makes better men, women, brothers, and sisters, to bring forth the nation unto the kingdom of God.

note.label: Genesis 45: Joseph Made Known unto His Brethren

precepts.why:
“The Lord said, Verily it shall be well with thy remnant; verily I will cause the enemy to entreat thee well in the time of evil and in the time of affliction.” To go from prison to governor over all the land of Egypt is that favor. The Lord caused the enemy to entreat Joseph well in the time of his affliction, and it was well with him.

The same favor is promised to the remnant in the time of evil. It comes by keeping the commandments, as Joseph did.

precepts.text: The Lord said, Verily I will cause the enemy to entreat thee well in the time of evil; the Most High delivers those he delights in.
precepts.point: The Lord rewarded David according to his righteousness and the cleanness of his hands, for he kept the ways of the Lord and did not wickedly depart from his God; all the Lord's judgments were before him and he did not depart from his statutes. He kept himself from his own iniquity, holding back his flesh; the one time it overtook him he was judged and got right back on track, for a righteous man falls and rises again.

note.label: 2 Samuel 22: The Lord Is My Rock and My Fortress

precepts.why:
“The Lord said, Verily it shall be well with thy remnant; verily I will cause the enemy to entreat thee well in the time of evil and in the time of affliction.” The Most High delivers those he delights in.

David sang, “He delivered me from my strong enemy, and from them that hated me: for they were too strong for me. They prevented me in the day of my calamity: but the Lord was my stay.” And, “He brought me forth also into a large place: he delivered me, because he delighted in me.”

The enemy was too strong for David, but in the time of evil the Lord was his stay and his help. When your ways please the Lord, he will deliver you.

precepts.text: The Most High says he will cause the enemy to entreat his remnant well in the time of evil; it is not that the heathen love Israel, but that the Lord moves a king or a friend to deal well with them.
precepts.point: The king grants him all this according to the good hand of his God upon him. Nehemiah had already prayed, and the Most High heard him and put it upon the king's heart to allow him to go.

note.label: Nehemiah 2: The King Sends Nehemiah to Rebuild

precepts.why:
Nehemiah asked the king for letters to the governors beyond the river and a letter to Asaph the keeper of the king's forest for timber, “And the king granted me, according to the good hand of my God upon me.” The Most High had said this would happen: “Verily it shall be well with thy remnant; verily I will cause the enemy to entreat thee well in the time of evil and in the time of affliction.”

It is not that the heathen love Israel. It is that the Lord causes the enemy to entreat his remnant well in the time of evil and affliction. Nehemiah had already prayed, and the Most High heard him and put it upon the king's heart to allow him to go. The king's favour was the good hand of God, not the king's own goodwill.

precepts.text: The words were found and eaten, becoming the joy and rejoicing of the heart, so this Bible should be our chief joy.
precepts.point: The Bible is the image of His goodness to His people, the Israelites. We are to live by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of the Most High, and eating the word means learning it.

note.label: Psalm 107: O Give Thanks unto the Lord

precepts.why:
“Thy words were found, and I did eat them; and thy word was unto me the joy and rejoicing of mine heart: for I am called by thy name, O Lord God of hosts.” Jeremiah ate the words of God, and eating the word means learning it.

That is how the hungry soul is filled with goodness: the words are found and eaten, and they become the joy and rejoicing of the heart. This Bible should be our chief joy, because we too are called by his name.

moments.label: Daily Bread for a Dying Man

points: Now what I want to stress is, the Lord showed Jeremiah there are some of our people that's just for death. Such as are for death, to death. Because Jeremiah, he's considered the weeping prophet. Jeremiah would weep over the hurt of the daughters of Zion, the atrocities that were done from Babylon of old. The same way many of us feel the same way in Babylon the great.
And such as are for the sword to the sword, and such as are for the famine to the famine, and such as are for the captivity to the captivity. That's some heavy stuff.

So we ask, and you see these atrocities like, man, why this keep happening to our people? It's happening because of what? Who knows why this stuff happens to us? Just yell it out. Because of what? Good. Everybody should have one consent: because we transgressed against the Lord our God. We transgressed against God.
Their widows are increased to me above the sand of the seas. So in Babylon, who has to be killed in order for there to be widows? The men. The men are being killed.

I have brought upon them against the mother of the young men a spoiler at noonday. It says God has brought a spoiler against the mother of young men. Isn't Nolan Wells's mother the mother of a young man? Listen, we got to understand who we transgressing against. He's the king of terrors.
She that hath borne seven languisheth. So, real quick, read that article.

So she was one of those widows that were left. The police choked him out allegedly for selling loose cigarettes on the street. I think they had six children. Six children. And she died that widow that was weeping because her husband was unjustly taken.

But God says, such are as death unto death. Everybody understand that? Meaning these things must happen, for the children of Israel. That's why we went the next chapter over: the children of Israel will begin to say, what is our transgression? What is our sin? As all these evils that's been pronounced against us come to pass.

How is it they can continually pervert judgment? How can we continually not get justice? The Lord has to keep turning it up. You think there's a lot of young men slain now? Just hold on, hang tight. Cause as our people get worse and worse, the Lord has to turn up that fire even more.

Thy words were found, and I did eat them; and thy word was unto me the joy and rejoicing of mine heart. You would think that is random, but it all ties back to their foundational understanding of what we read in Deuteronomy and Exodus. Jeremiah understood this.

note.label: Daily Bread for a Dying Man

points: Though Moses and Samuel stood before Him, the mind of the Most High could not be toward this people; He says cast them out of My sight.

When the people ask where they shall go, the answer is such as are for death to death, for the sword to the sword, for the famine to the famine, and for the captivity to the captivity. That is how we got removed from before the Most High.

He appoints four kinds over them: the sword to slay, the dogs to tear, and the fowls and beasts to devour, and He will remove them into all kingdoms of the earth because of what Manasseh son of Hezekiah did in Jerusalem.

He is weary with repenting and will bereave them of children because they return not from their ways; the mother of young men gets a spoiler at noonday, and she that bore seven languishes and gives up the ghost.
Jeremiah cries woe over being born a man of strife and contention, cursed by everyone though he lent to no one on usury. The Most High answers that it shall be well with his remnant.

That remnant is those who are keeping the commandments. Their substance and treasures will be given to the spoil for all their sins, and they will pass with their enemies into a land they do not know.
Jeremiah asks the Most High to remember him, visit him, and revenge him of his persecutors, and not to take him away in His longsuffering, since for His sake he has suffered rebuke.
His words were found and Jeremiah did eat them, and they were the joy and rejoicing of his heart, for he is called by the name of the Most High and sat alone, filled with indignation.

He asks why his pain is perpetual and his wound refuses to be healed. This is what the prophets go through: we bring healing, order, structure and discipline to our people and get hated and treated badly, and sometimes these are the thoughts we have.
If Jeremiah returns, the Most High will bring him again to stand before Him; if he takes the precious from the vile he shall be as His mouth. Let them return to him, but he is not to return to them.
He will make Jeremiah a fenced brazen wall; they shall fight against him but not prevail, for the Most High is with him to save and deliver him.

That is what we live on. When we go out teaching this bible, and when brothers and sisters apply the commandments to their everyday lives, people will come against us, but the Most High is our defense. As long as we keep the commandments and the faith of Christ, no one can prevail, and if they try they will fail.
